rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Only one file-only chunk (chunk 1) exists beyond the title slide, so all referents must resolve within it plus its own header. Closest call: line 5 "The loops drawn across them all run the same shape" — "them" has no separate antecedent sentence of its own, but the chunk's own header ("...maps onto the same six phases") plus the immediately preceding clause ("maps onto the same cycle") jointly establish the referent before the pronoun fires; a reader holding the header resolves "them" to the cycle's six phases. Every other pronoun ("it" in the Context/Work bullets referring to "the agent", "the result" in Verification/Absorption referring to the immediately-prior Work/Verification bullet, "several" in the closing sentence referring to "the phases") resolves against material stated earlier in the same six-bullet list, which is cumulative in-chunk context, not a forward or cross-file pointer.

Chunk 1 opens with fresh content ("Every piece of agentic work maps onto the same cycle...") rather than any backward pointer at another slide or file. No construction of the form "the opening lecture said" / "that story" / "as discussed" appears anywhere in the body (lines 1-17). This is the training's first map reveal (per the maintainer's Placement note), so there is nothing upstream in this training for it to point at even informally.

Chunk 1 carries a lede sentence, the map figure, six developed definition bullets, and a closing generalization ("The phases are places, not a pipeline. A real task sits in several at once.") — a fully self-carrying claim on its own, not a wait-state or single context-dependent bullet. Chunk 0 is the bare H1 title slide ("# The whole map", no lede before the `##`); by the template's own convention this is prior context for chunk 1, not itself evaluated as an orphan candidate.

Header "Every task maps onto the same six phases" (line 3) is literally verified by the chunk's own content: exactly six bolded bullet leads follow (Intent, Context, Work, Verification, Absorption, Outcome), and the closing sentence reaffirms "The phases are places...". Header + bolded leads read as a true summary under the sequential read; nothing in the chunk contradicts the header's count or claim.

Checked all six sub-items against chunk 1: no "Not X. Not Y. Z." construction anywhere; no anaphora/epistrophe triple (the six bullets are structurally parallel as a definition list, which is the list format itself, not a repeated rhetorical construction on one slide); no self-grading superlative (nothing like "one of the most useful moves"); no number-plus-retraction (the count "six phases" is stated plainly once, never hedged or walked back); no abstraction-noun stack (bullet prose is plain — "What you point the work at", "How you know the result is any good" — not stacked abstractions); the verb triplet in the Work bullet ("acts, reads the result, corrects, goes again") has every verb answer "what does this concretely mean?" on its own (perform an action / read what happened / adjust / repeat) — no empty leg.
